organization: Above and Beyond Family Recovery Center
program: Free outpatient addiction counseling and recovery support

what: Above and Beyond provides free outpatient substance-use counseling on Chicago's West Side.
Case managers also help clients access employment, housing and medical referrals.
The revised annual-work illustration includes short morbidity effects and signed household resources.
strengths: Reports annual group participation and concrete employment/housing outputs.
Free patient access reduces direct fee barriers.
Historical audited costs include recognized donated resources.
reservations: Recovery has no defined denominator or causal comparison.
2024 cost versus2023 output is not current productivity.
Net earnings, housing welfare and gift-created capacity remain unmeasured.

sections.what: Free Level I/II outpatient counseling and referral operate at 2942 W Lake Street, Chicago (Cook County, current MSA). Medical linkage is not evidence of universal medication treatment. Pantry is a sister organization. [Protocol](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/how-we-do-it/clinical-protocol/)
sections.monitoring: 2023 snapshot reports 1,058 group participants and 42.9% recovered, without definition or denominator. Applying that rate to group participants is judgment; validity factor 0.5 reduces it but cannot validate the unknown denominator. Project MATCH compared active alcohol therapies, not treatment versus none; it does not supply this recipient's causal effect. Request validated utility, retention and counterfactual recovery. [Snapshot](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/donate/annual-report/) [Original trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8979210/) Fresh review confirms five successfully employed out of62 employment assistance recipients,19 supportive-housing enrollments and three former-patient job offers. Offers are not added to jobs. These are descriptive, not causal or retained outcomes.
sections.qualitative: Clinical welfare uses1058patients, while .8household grouping affects resources only. Housing/referral channels remain unquantified, notzero. Five observed jobs anchor a judged .3additionality*.5retention cohort with $1000disposable gain after taxes, benefit withdrawal and work/care costs. Positive-only .5overlap and full$10net incremental time/access burden are hypotheses relative to alternatives, not observed gains or gross salaries.
sections.cost: Use all $4,296,413 audited 2024 expenses, not the $3,526,474 tax summary. Includes $572,432 recognized donated resources and gross event costs. A $1,000 whole-portfolio equivalent corresponds to 0.246 group participants before response/additionality/geography, not actual marginal admission cost. Six-month utility gain is judged, no survival effect. [Original audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000386319) The audit separately nets a $50,786 loss on transfer of assets against revenue. It is outside the operating-expense numerator; including it as a broader accounting-cost sensitivity gives $4,347,199. This is not an omitted recurring treatment cost. Revision removes the separate .3gift-financing factor from annual work, without claiming gift capacity. Full aggregate .05QALY-equivalent process harm is a judgment. Signed resources are negative centrally (−.19227), with health3.18641; price approximately$14.35M per ten combined equivalents. Whole cost against partial quantified channels is not portfolio expected value. Matched2023 snapshotcost$3,446,320 and program-only cost are sensitivities, not verified allocations.
sections.funding: 2024 original audit: support/revenue $5,078,619; program expense $3,231,072, management $756,564, fundraising $308,777; net assets $2,355,942; cash $1,892,947. Program fees $2,390,278, deferred grant $585,104 and note payable $850,000 complicate liquidity. Gift is unrestricted portfolio support; Marginal financing and capacity remain unknown; they are not another annual-work multiplier. Marketing that operating costs are covered does not establish zero overhead or entirely additional health. [Audit](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2024-12-GSAFAC-0000386319) [Giving](https://aboveandbeyondfrc.org/donate/) Root independently freshly retrieved the original31-page audit and checked financial pages6–7 on October7; historical2024 cost remains paired with2023 service scale. The .429*.5 clinical response hypothesis is not validated by the missing denominator. Distinct global provider/payer costs appear only in sensitivity and are not duplicated with recognized in-kind already in C. Other cash/housing resources remain unknown, not implicitly absent.

model.costScope: Historical2024 audited whole annual expense against2023 service-scale hypotheses; Root freshly checked original financial pages6–7. Partial channel, not full portfolio EV or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Chicago Cook County site; g=.95 judged, not observed residence.
model.formula: Health=g*(N*p*v*a*u*T-full process harm)/(1+r)^delay; resource=.5*sum(people*discounted years*log(after/before)*localshare) with joint flows and positive-only overlap; price10=10*C/(health+signed resource).
model.counterfactual: Alternative clinical care via a; employment additionality and retention separate; unknown marginal financing not another annual multiplier.
model.attribution: Recovery percentage lacks denominator. Utility, job causal share and disposable gains are judgments. Full negative costs and harms persist on benefit failure.
model.uncertainty: Very weak clinical attribution; current volume and response definition unknown. The central estimate is an illustrative scenario, not a calibrated expected value; favorable/poor scenarios are not statistical confidence bounds. Service location establishes eligibility, while modeled MSA residency shares remain unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Incremental response equivalents, .10 utility for .5 years central.
